title: Compare two data sets and spot a trend

slides.title: Two launchers, one question
slides.text: Two launchers stand side by side on the Test Range. Launcher B seems to send its probes farther, but every landing varies a little. Tally wants to know whether the difference is real or just the usual scatter, and how launch power and distance go together.

slides.title: How far apart, in spreads
slides.text: Put the two box plots over one number line. B's median is 21 meters and A's is 15, so they are 6 meters apart. Both boxes are 4 meters wide, so the medians are 6 ÷ 4 = 1.5 box widths apart. The two boxes do not even overlap: B's probes really do go farther.

visual.label: Landings of launchers A and B

focus.cue: B's median is 21 meters: 6 meters farther.
B's box is 23 − 19 = 4 meters wide, the same as A's.

slides.title: Means apart, counted in MADs
slides.text: When two data sets vary by about the same amount, divide the gap between their means by that spread. The answer says how many spreads apart they are.

slides.title: A scatter plot and its trend
slides.text: Each point is one launch: its power across, its distance up. The points rise from left to right, a positive association. A trend line runs close to the points, with about as many above it as below. One point sits far below the rest: an outlier, a probe that hit a rock.

focus.cue: The points rise from left to right: a positive association.
The trend line runs close to the points.
This point is far below the pattern: an outlier.

slides.title: A random sample speaks for the batch
slides.text: Testing every probe in a batch of 300 takes too long, so Tally tests a random sample of 20. Four of the 20 need a new fin. That is a rate of 4 ÷ 20 = 0.2, so about 0.2 × 300 = 60 probes in the batch need one. A random sample gives every probe the same chance of being picked.

words.means: how two quantities go together: up together, one up and one down, or no pattern
a straight line drawn close to the points of a scatter plot
a value far from the rest of the data
a part of a group picked so that every member has the same chance

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Launch Lab at Trend Watch. Compare two launchers, estimate a batch from a sample, read the pattern of a scatter plot, find its outlier and predict from a trend line. A wrong plan shows you what it really gives.
